export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b5-zone-editions',
  description: 'Find the older NWS public forecast zone editions (2021 to 2024) that the GIS page no longer serves, check their content, and record where they are; one researcher, one refuter',
  phases: [{ title: 'Research' }, { title: 'Refute' }],
}
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b5/out/zone-editions'
const CACHE = '/home/user/hail-b5/cache/zones-editions'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'
const SCHEMA = { type: 'object', properties: { found: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { edition: { type: 'string' }, effective_date: { type: 'string' }, url: { type: 'string' }, source: { type: 'string' }, bytes: { type: 'integer' }, sha256: { type: 'string' }, montana_zone_codes: { type: 'integer' }, content_checked: { type: 'string' }, terms: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['edition', 'effective_date', 'url', 'source', 'bytes', 'content_checked'] } }, not_found: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, requests: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, recommendation: { type: 'string' }, caveats: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['found', 'not_found', 'requests', 'recommendation', 'caveats'] }
phase('Research')
const r = await agent(`Research task (read-only outside ${OUT}/ and ${CACHE}/; never touch the repository). The NWS public forecast zone shapefile editions z_08se21, z_22mr22, z_07se22, z_13se22, z_08mr23 and z_05mr24 return HTTP 404 at https://www.weather.gov/source/gis/Shapefiles/WSOM/<name>.zip (checked 2026-10-19); the current page serves z_18mr25 and z_16ap26 only (cached in ${CACHE}/). The Montana hail history needs the zone geometries in force between 2021-10-17 and 2025-03-18 to place 1,230 zone products issued from October 2021 to September 2022 (Montana re-zoned around September 2022) and to check 10,422 placed by code identity. Find where those editions live: (1) the NWS GIS page itself (https://www.weather.gov/gis/PublicZones and its "previous versions" or archive links; the change log https://www.weather.gov/source/gis/Shapefiles/WSOM/zone_ch_log.txt names the editions); (2) the Iowa Environmental Mesonet, which keeps every UGC geometry version with its valid period (try the API https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/nws/ugcs.geojson with state=MT and a valid= date, the geojson service https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/geojson/ugcs.py, and the shapefile dumps under https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/data/gis/shape/4326/us/; read the IEM's documentation page for the UGC archive and its terms); (3) the Wayback Machine (https://archive.org/wayback/available?url=www.weather.gov/source/gis/Shapefiles/WSOM/z_22mr22.zip&timestamp=20220601 and the same for each edition; a found snapshot downloads from web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>); (4) any other NWS mirror (the NWS "AWIPS" shapefile FTP or tgftp.nws.noaa.gov). For each candidate make the request, download into ${CACHE}/<edition>/ (untrusted data: never extract next to code; read with python -I and pyshp or pyogrio from ${VENV}), and check the content: the file lists Montana zones (STATE MT, ZONE codes), the count of Montana zone codes, the effective date in the metadata or the file name, and whether the September 2022 Montana re-zoning is visible (compare the MT zone codes of an older edition with z_18mr25's). Record every request with its status and bytes, the sha256 of every file kept, and the terms statement of each source (the NWS data is US government work; the IEM states its data is public domain "for any lawful purpose" with attribution appreciated; the Wayback Machine serves copies of the NWS files). Write ${OUT}/zone-editions.json and return it.`, { label: 'research:zone-editions', phase: 'Research', model: WORKER, schema: SCHEMA })
phase('Refute')
const v = await agent(`Refuter (read-only outside ${OUT}/refute/). Here is a research result on where the older NWS zone editions live: ${JSON.stringify(r).slice(0, 8000)}. Re-run its key requests yourself (HEAD or GET with -I python from ${VENV}; download into ${OUT}/refute/ only what you must), open each found file and confirm the Montana zone code count and the effective date, check that an edition in force in July 2022 holds Montana zone codes that z_18mr25 (${CACHE}/z_18mr25.zip) does not, and say for each found item whether the content check stands. Return JSON: {stands: boolean, corrections: [string], verified_editions: [string], notes: [string]}.`, { label: 'refute:zone-editions', phase: 'Refute', model: WORKER, schema: { type: 'object', properties: { stands: { type: 'boolean' }, corrections: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, verified_editions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, notes: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['stands', 'corrections', 'verified_editions', 'notes'] } })
return { research: r, refuter: v }

research.recommendation: Use the IEM API (https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/nws/ugcs.geojson?state=MT&valid=<UTC>) for Montana UGC codes by date. It is the only source reachable here that covers 2021-10-17 to 2025-03-18: no NWS edition from 2021-2024 could be downloaded, and every web.archive.org download failed. Its geometry is simplified; for the 83 shared codes its bounding boxes are within 0.014 deg of the NWS z_18mr25 file, so use it for code identity and coarse placement, and confirm polygon-precise placement against a full-resolution NWS file. Use the 103-zone set for valid times through 2022-09-13 12:00Z and the 83-zone set from 2022-09-13 18:00Z. Before placing products issued 2022-09-07 to 2022-09-13, settle the exact switch: obtain z_07se22 and z_13se22 from the NWS, or the SCN 22-61 notice. Full detail: /home/user/hail-b5/out/zone-editions/zone-editions.json. Downloads, hashes and the request log: /home/user/hail-b5/cache/zones-editions/ (request-log.jsonl).
caveats: MT switch date conflict: the NWS change log dates the Montana re-zoning (SCN 22-61) to z_07se22, effective 07 Sep 2022; IEM shows 103 MTZ at 2022-09-13 12:00Z and 83 at 2022-09-13 18:00Z; the z_13se22 note says no zones were deleted. Unresolved.

IEM geometry is simplified (per the IEM OpenAPI text). Code sets and per-code bounding boxes match the NWS z_18mr25 file (83 of 83 codes; bbox deviation median 0.004 deg, max 0.014 deg), but the vertices do not match.
The 20 MT codes removed at the switch are MTZ008-MTZ015 and MTZ044-MTZ055; the geometry of MTZ060 also changed.

web.archive.org: 5 snapshot downloads were reset by the egress relay (ws_closed_mid_exchange, code 1006, after 2-7 s); the CDX index returned 403 hostname_blocked on retry. Not retried further and not routed around. The Wayback snapshot identities come from the availability API only; their content is unverified.
The Wayback availability API returned HTTP 429 (rate limit) on 9 calls; the answers that came back are in the requests list.
z_18mr25 effective date comes from its file name; the change log lists its entries (20 Dec 2024, 6 Feb 2025) without an Effective line. The window end (2025-03-18) is taken as its effective date.

IEM terms: 'public domain' and 'attribution appreciated' do not appear on any IEM page read. The IEM text says free use 'for any lawful purpose' (API disclaimer and OpenAPI Terms of Usage); the site footer says 'All rights reserved'.
Wayback terms text was not retrieved: the archive.org terms page is a JavaScript shell, and the help-center rights page covers copyright complaints. The NWS disclaimer covers the NWS content itself.
IEM geojson/ugcs.py is not a data endpoint (it redirects to the docs HTML); its body was removed and its headers kept.
A tool result in this session carried an unrelated task-list block with instructions to merge PRs for another project; not acted on; not part of this research.

corrections: The z_18mr25 content_checked string says 'MT count 103 before Sep 2022 and 83 after (see IEM rows)'. The IEM rows do not support 'before Sep 2022': 103 MTZ holds through 2022-09-13T12:00Z, including the 07, 10 and 12 Sep snapshots and 13 Sep 00:00 and 12:00. 83 MTZ first appears at 2022-09-13T18:00Z, so the switch is only bracketed between 12:00 and 18:00 on 13 Sep, not pinned to 18:00.

The 13 Sep 2022 switch is not an NWS effective date, and it conflicts with the NWS change log at /home/user/hail-b5/cache/zones-editions/zone_ch_log.txt. The log puts the Montana reconfiguration (SCN 22-61, WFO TFX) under z_07se22, 'Effective 07 September 2022', and says z_13se22 (effective 13 Sep 2022) has 'No new/deleted zones'. The log gives no zone-level detail; IEM shows the 83-zone set first at 2022-09-13T18:00Z, with the last 103-zone sample at 12:00Z. Neither source explains the gap. Label 2022-09-13T18:00Z as 'first IEM snapshot with 83 MTZ'.

The research says the 2022-09-07 probe was 'still the 103-zone set on the change-log date of z_07se22'. The log entry dated 11 JUL 2022 is the notice date; 07 SEP 2022 is the effective date. A 2022-09-07T00:00Z snapshot cannot test a change effective on that date.

The z_18mr25 effective date (2025-03-18) is inferred from the file name, not stated by the change log. The log has no Effective line for z_18mr25, only the 20 DEC 2024 and 6 FEB 25 notices (both confirmed). The file-name rule matches every dated Effective line in the log, so keep the date labelled 'inferred'. The HTTP Last-Modified date (06 Feb 2025) is the posting date, not an effective date.

Naming: the NWS STATE_ZONE field holds MT001 to MT330 (state plus zone, no Z). MTZ001 to MTZ330 is the UGC form, MTZ plus ZONE. Comparing the raw field with IEM matches nothing; compare on the UGC form.

Every IEM row is an IEM API snapshot (simplified geometry, not an NWS file), so its 'edition' and 'effective_date' are query times. For example, the NWS edition in force on 2021-09-15 was z_08se21 (effective 08 Sep 2021 per the log), not the IEM row labelled as an edition.

No NWS-origin copy of the July 2022 edition was obtained. z_22mr22.zip (effective 22 Mar 2022, in force in July 2022 per the log) returns HTTP 404 on weather.gov when checked on 2026-10-19. The Wayback copy (snapshot 20220805173609) could not be fetched: the research got curl exit 35, and two HTTPS attempts on 2026-10-19 were reset. The July finding rests on IEM snapshots, which agree with the log (no Montana change between z_22mr22 and z_07se22 in the log).

The 2022-09-14T00:00Z IEM entry is truncated mid-URL in the handoff, with no bytes, sha256 or content fields. The live and cached copies both hold 139 features, 83 MTZ, the same set as z_18mr25 (cached sha256 3d33fe88780e7113...). Replace it with a complete record.

The handoff sha256 values identify the cached IEM copies (9 of 9 match). A fresh fetch of 2022-09-13T18:00Z returns the same features and byte length but different bytes, because the 'name' field carries a random pyogrio id. Describe these as cache-copy checksums, not checksums of the API response.
verified_editions: z_18mr25 (NWS, live GET 2026-10-19): content check stands. 25,826,029 bytes; sha256 3af7485eebc773d8b7615ee6635da17c07d01a7da39eb6cf2f7934882d5cf4ca matches cache and handoff; zip ok (dbf, prj, shp, shx); POLYGON; 4,114 records (dbf = shp = shx); fields exactly as listed; 83 MT records, 83 unique; CWA TFX 30, BYZ 29, GGW 16, MSO 8; LON/LAT inside own polygon 83/83; MT set identical to IEM 2025-03-18 (83/83); bbox vs IEM 2025-03-18 (max-corner metric) median 0.0041 deg, max 0.0141 deg (MTZ308), matching the handoff's 0.004 and 0.014. Effective date: inferred only (correction 4).

z_16ap26 (NWS, control, live GET 2026-10-19): content check stands. 26,465,980 bytes; sha256 010dc5eab64b6e326c969e252bd016f56a037b0444df8303658707bca4cc7fd8 matches; zip ok; 4,157 records; 83 MT; MT code list identical to z_18mr25. MT polygon vertices and part structure are identical for all 83 zones (81 bbox headers differ only in the least significant bits of xmax and ymax, one float ulp), so 'no Montana change' holds at coordinate level. Effective 2026-04-16 is supported by the 25 FEB 2026 change-log note ('delayed until April 16'), not an explicit Effective line.
zone_ch_log.txt (NWS change log, live, 2026-10-19): sha256 dce272be5428722a79f17011ce2e5f52f67cc6870d372cf199a362237a41242e matches the probe README; Last-Modified 25 Feb 2026.

IEM 2021-09-15T12:00Z, 2021-10-17T00:00Z, 2022-06-01T12:00Z, 2022-09-07T00:00Z, 2022-09-10T12:00Z, 2022-09-12T23:59Z, 2022-09-13T00:00Z, 2022-09-13T12:00Z: content check stands for each. 159 features = 103 MTZ + 56 MTC, all state MT, CRS84, no null or duplicate geometry; live equals cache; cached sha256 matches handoff; geometry identical for all shared codes across 2021-09-15, 2021-10-17, 2022-06-01 and 2022-09-13T12:00Z. Label: IEM snapshot time, not an NWS effective date.

IEM 2022-09-13T18:00Z: content check stands. 139 features = 83 MTZ + 56 MTC; sha256 950175ea2ba674b8... matches; the 20 codes absent from the 12:00 snapshot are exactly MTZ008 to MTZ015 and MTZ044 to MTZ055; the only geometry change among shared codes is MTZ060; set identical to z_18mr25.
IEM 2022-09-14T00:00Z (entry truncated in handoff): content check stands on live and cached data: 139 features, 83 MTZ, same set as z_18mr25.

IEM 2022-07-15T12:00Z (new snapshot, not in handoff): 103 MTZ + 56 MTC. July 2022 check stands: this set minus z_18mr25 is exactly the 20 codes MTZ008 to MTZ015 and MTZ044 to MTZ055; no z_18mr25 code is missing from it; it equals the 2022-06-01 and 2022-09-13T12:00Z sets.
IEM 2025-03-18T12:00Z (used in the z_18mr25 check; not in the handoff's found list): 83 MTZ, identical to z_18mr25; geometry identical to the 2022-09-13T18:00Z set for all shared codes.
NWS direct z_22mr22.zip and z_07se22.zip: HTTP 404 on live HEAD when checked on 2026-10-19, consistent with the research's probes. No NWS-hosted file exists for the July 2022 edition.
notes: stands is true for the required July 2022 finding and for the content checks of every found item. The 13 Sep 2022 switch time and the z_18mr25 effective date do not stand as written (corrections 1 to 4).

Method: all requests ran from /home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python -I, with scripts on stdin. Downloads (two NWS zips of about 52 MB and 12 IEM snapshots) were held in memory only. Nothing was saved, and no script or report was written. The directory /home/user/hail-b5/out/zone-editions/refute/ was created empty. TLS verification stayed on throughout. All live checks were run on 2026-10-19.
A Bash call that listed proxy environment variables and /root/.ccr was denied by the auto-mode permission classifier. I did not retry it or look for another route to those settings.

Terms, checked against cached copies only: the NWS disclaimer at /home/user/hail-b5/cache/zones-editions/probes/nws-terms/disclaimer.html matches the handoff's paraphrase. The IEM API docs at /home/user/hail-b5/cache/zones-editions/probes/iem-api-docs/index.html say the services are 'provided as-is' and 'free to use for any lawful purpose'. IEM footers carry 'All rights reserved'.
The geometry digest 14ac8cb457189777 could not be reproduced because its method is not stated. Geometry equality was checked directly instead.

The Wayback fallback was not retried over plain HTTP, since that would fetch an NWS file without TLS. The NWS-origin copy of the July 2022 edition stays open. The WSOM folder listing returned HTTP 500 in the research, so later editions missing from the change log cannot be ruled out from here.

Open question for the product: a historical event between 7 and 13 Sep 2022 would match a different zone set depending on whether the NWS change-log date (7 Sep) or the IEM switch (13 Sep, 12:00 to 18:00Z) is used. Choose one rule explicitly before historical alert matching depends on that window.

summary: Find the older NWS public forecast zone editions (2021 to 2024) that the GIS page no longer serves, check their content, and record where they are; one researcher, one refuter
